text: After this you can present findings with their supporting observations, limits, and follow-up.

A decision-ready audit report shows what was observed, how each saving was calculated, what it may cost, and which uncertainties remain. Historical records describe patterns; field measurements and interviews help explain them. Where staff accounts conflict with controls or meter trends, document both and investigate. State projected results as estimates, identify verification tasks, and distinguish learning exercises from practical site qualifications.

items: Name the operating problem and candidate measure. You should see: One clear claim per measure. If not: Separate observations from hypotheses.
Show baseline, units, costs, and assumptions. You should see: Reproducible savings arithmetic. If not: Label data that must be collected.
Record risks and interacting measures. You should see: Limits beside the recommendation. If not: Avoid adding mutually overlapping savings.
Recommend verification and follow-up. You should see: A test or monitoring action. If not: Leave unverified savings as estimates.
Inferred: Illustrative case: A fan schedule says off overnight, but a meter log shows continuing consumption. Log the disagreement and check control operation before crediting any energy saving.

text: Write recommendations so another auditor can repeat the calculation.
A clean report cannot replace missing site evidence.
